quotes.R2: The finance manager shall approve any refund over 500
quotes.R5: The team leader shall approve any refund over 400

what: A refund over 500 is also over 400, so two people are told to approve it, with two different deadlines, and nothing says whose approval counts.
impact: Nobody knows whose approval counts, so large refunds wait while two people each assume the other has it.

quotes.R6: delete refund records 7 years after the refund is paid
quotes.R7: keep the approval record for every refund for the life of the client account

what: An approval record is part of the refund record, so it must be both deleted after 7 years and kept for as long as the account is open.
impact: For any account open longer than 7 years the system has to break one of the two rules.

what: Nothing says who approves a refund from 50 to 400.
open_question: Is a refund from 50 to 400 meant to need no approval, or is a rule missing?

quotes.R8: send the customer a text message when the refund is paid

what: Both tell the customer about the refund, so one looked like a repeat of the other.
reason: R1 is about the decision and R8 is about the payment. They happen at different times and the customer needs both.

what: The person asking for the refund is a customer in R1 and a client in R7.
impact: A reader may take client and customer for two different groups and build two sets of records.
who_decides: Business analyst, with the glossary owner
what_changed: The glossary agreed since the first review lists customer only, so client is no longer an accepted name.
